message.content: In this SvelteKit expense tracker, receipt images are stored in a private Supabase bucket and displayed via signed URLs. I need to understand the performance characteristics of how images load on the list pages. Be very thorough and quote actual code. Investigate: 1. The `getSignedReceiptUrl()` helper in src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts — show it in full. Does it make a network round-trip to Supabase per call? Does it batch? Is there caching? 2. On the receipts list page (src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte): how are signed URLs loaded for the list? Find the `signedUrls` reactive map and the `$effect` that populates it. Is a signed URL generated for EVERY receipt in the list, or only visible ones? Is it done in a loop? Sequentially or in parallel (Promise.all)? Quote the code. 3. Same question for the expenses list page (src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte) — does it load thumbnail/preview images for every expense row? 4. Same for transactions page — does it show images at all? 5. Are the images rendered as tags with the signed URL as src for every row? Is there any lazy loading (loading="lazy"), thumbnails, or image resizing? Or does each row load the full-size original image? 6. Is there any thumbnail generation anywhere, or only full-resolution originals stored? 7. How big is the signed-URL generation cost — is each call an individual supabase.storage.from().createSignedUrl() call (one HTTP request each), or is there a createSignedUrls (plural, batch) call? Report file paths and code snippets. I specifically want to know: for a page with N receipts, how many signed-URL network calls and how many image downloads happen on load, and whether they're parallelized or lazy.
